subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Marathon Majors Society is a running club.
• One of the main goals among club members is to complete all six World Marathon Majors.
• Those who achieve this are called Six Star Finishers.
• Michelle Wong became a Six Star Finisher on April 17, 2016.
• The Berlin Marathon in Germany was established in 1974.
• The Boston Marathon in the USA was established in 1897.
prompt: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to explain the Six Star Finishers running challenge to a new audience?

choices.A: If you are looking for a new running challenge, consider joining the Marathon Majors Society, as did Michelle Wong, a runner who successfully completed all six World Marathon Majors.
choices.B: Not until after you have completed all six World Marathon Majors—including the Berlin Marathon in Germany and the Boston Marathon in the USA—can you include yourself among the Six Star Finishers of the Marathon Majors Society.
choices.C: On April 17, 2016, Michelle Wong finally completed the feat of finishing all six World Marathon Majors, including the Berlin Marathon in Germany and the Boston Marathon in the USA.
choices.D: Runners aiming to count themselves among the Six Star Finishers must complete not only the Berlin Marathon but also the Boston Marathon.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it most effectively explains the Six Star Finishers challenge to a new audience by providing all essential elements of the challenge in a single, coherent statement. The sentence clearly defines the specific requirement (completing 'all six World Marathon Majors'), names the designation earned ('Six Star Finishers'), connects it to the organizing body ('Marathon Majors Society'), and provides concrete examples of included marathons (Berlin and Boston). This comprehensive approach gives newcomers a complete understanding of what the challenge entails and what achievement it represents.
